name: Sub tasks management
description:
1. **Scope:** analyzed how codx-junior manages sub-tasks and how a model can run them in parallel, aiming to let a profile decompose complex issues into simple parallel tasks.
2. **Data model is done:** every task is a `Chat` with `parent_id`/`child_index`, `board`/`column`, `status`+`status_history`, `cost`, `pr_view` — the full task tree already exists in `db.py`/`chat_manager.py`.
3. **Fan-out is done:** `engine/chat_engine_actions.py::generate_tasks` asks the AI for a JSON task list and creates child chats in parallel via `asyncio.gather`, with live status reporting — but it's only reachable via REST/Socket.IO, not from a model.
4. **Blocking defects:** `generate_tasks` calls sync `AI.chat()` inside a running loop (silently swallowed `RuntimeError`), `process_task(wait=True)` returns "completed" before doing anything, tools run sequentially (max 5/round), and no concurrency limit, fan-in, worktree isolation, or task tools ship in any profile.
5. **Gap / next step:** missing `create_tasks` / `task_status` / `wait_for_tasks` tools plus a worktree-per-task option — fix the two bugs first, then add the trio.

Analyze subtask management and find tools and ways a model can run parallel tasks. Report findings, status (done, draft implementation, not working stuff)

We want to allow a profile to generate parallel tasks to break complex issues into simple ones.

I'll analyze the codebase to understand subtask management and identify ways a model can run parallel tasks.Now let me read the key task-related tool files.Let me read the full `generate_tasks` implementation and find the agent tool runtime.# Subtask Management & Parallel Task Execution — Findings **Objective:** understand how tasks/sub-tasks work today, what lets a model run them in parallel, and what is missing to let a **profile generate parallel tasks** that break a complex issue into simple ones. **Status legend** | Icon | Meaning | |---|---| | ✅ | Working / done | | 🟡 | Draft implementation — code exists, incomplete or untested edge cases | | ❌ | Not working (or only usable on a path nobody calls) | | 🧱 | Missing — no implementation found | --- ## 1. Mental model There is **one** unit of work in codx-junior: the **`Chat`**. ```mermaid flowchart TD P[Parent Chat
complex issue] -->|parent_id| C1[Chat / Task 1] P -->|parent_id| C2[Chat / Task 2] P -->|parent_id| C3[Chat / Task 3] C1 --> M1[mode: chat · board/column · pr_view · cost] C2 --> M1 C3 --> M1 ``` From `codx/junior/db.py` (`Chat`), each task-chat carries its own: | Field | Role in task management | |---|---| | `parent_id`, `child_index` | tree of tasks (parent → sub-tasks) | | `board`, `column`, `kanban_id` | Kanban placement (defaults `kanban` / `tasks`) | | `mode` | `chat` \| `task` \| `agent` \| `vibe` \| `tutorial` — changes prompt behaviour | | `status` + `status_history` | append-only status transitions (cycle time / throughput metrics) | | `priority`, `due_date`, `progress`, `assignees`, `sort_index`, `sprints` | planning metadata | | `cost`, `estimation_cost` | per-task AI budget (SmolAgent stops at the limit) | | `branch`, `pr_view` | git isolation per task (`branch` field is declared but **never written**) | | `ignore_parent_knowledge`, `ignore_parent_files` | context isolation from parent | So the *data model* for parallel tasks already exists. What is missing is the **orchestration** (fan-out/fan-in) and the **tool surface** for a model/profile. --- ## 2. Inventory of what exists | # | Capability | Location | Status | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | AI splits a chat into a JSON task list | `engine/chat_engine_actions.py::generate_tasks` | 🟡 implemented, **blocking bug** (see §4.1) | | 2 | **Parallel** creation of child task-chats | same (`asyncio.gather`) | ✅ | | 3 | Live status message with per-task table + timings | `TaskGenerationStatus` / `SubTaskStatus` | ✅ | | 4 | Child corrects/expands description from parent context | `process_sub_task` prompt + `get_chat_analysis_parents` | ✅ | | 5 | Entry points for humans | `POST /api/chats/sub-tasks`, SIO `codx-junior-subtasks`, `codx-junior-generate-tasks` | ✅ | | 6 | LLM tool `create_task` | `tools/create_task_tool.py` | 🟡 draft (defects §4.2) | | 7 | LLM tool `process_task` (`wait` flag) | `tools/process_task_tool.py` | 🟡 **`wait=True` does not wait** (§4.3) | | 8 | Sub-task generation **as a tool** for a model | — | 🧱 missing | | 9 | List/inspect child task status as a tool | — | 🧱 missing | | 10 | Fan-in: wait for all children and aggregate | — | 🧱 missing | | 11 | Per-task working-tree isolation (branch/worktree) | `tools/git_tools.py` (`create_pr_branch(worktree=True)`) | 🟡 primitives exist, **not wired to tasks** | | 12 | Parallel execution of tools **inside** one agent round | `ai/smol/smol_agent.py::_run_chat_loop` | ❌ sequential | | 13 | Concurrency limit / semaphore / global fan-out budget | — | 🧱 missing (only `LoopGuard` breadth 5/round) | | 14 | Legacy `TaskManager` | `task_manager.py` | ❌ broken import + unreferenced | | 15 | Embedded issue→subtask agent | `agents/git_issues_agent.py::create_subtasks` | ❌ returns a hardcoded list | --- ## 3. Path A — chat-level sub-task generation (the real implementation) `codx/junior/engine/chat_engine_actions.py::generate_tasks` is the only end-to-end sub-task mechanism. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[generate_tasks chat, instructions] --> B[status message phase=starting] B --> C[summarize_chat → content] C --> D[phase=analyzing · prompt asks for JSON task list] D --> E{extract_json_blocks ok?} E -- no --> F[retry x2 → phase=error] E -- yes --> G[SubTaskStatus per task · phase=creating] G --> H["asyncio.gather(process_sub_task ...) in parallel"] H --> I[each: new Chat parent_id=chat.id
board/column/project inherited · mode=chat] I --> J[chat_with_project → AI rewrites description] J --> K[save_chat + chat_event created] K --> L[phase=done · status message re-rendered] ``` Notable implementation details: - The prompt instructs *"ONLY generate the JSON task list"*, names must be prioritised (`"Task 1: Perform analysis"`), descriptions must be self-sufficient. - `instructions` parameter is appended to the prompt — that is the hook a profile could use to shape decomposition. - Each sub-task inherits `profiles` and `files` from the **last message** (`last_message.profiles` / `last_message.files`), so the child runs under the same profile/tools as the parent. - The parent chat keeps a single `task_item="status"` assistant message that is re-rendered and broadcast as tasks progress. - `mode` is set to **`"chat"`** here (the older `engine.py` copy set `"task"` / `"vibe"`). --- ## 4. Findings — what is broken or fragile ### 4.1 ❌ `generate_tasks` calls the **synchronous** `AI.chat()` inside a coroutine ```py # chat_engine_actions.py::generate_tasks (async def) while retry_count: retry_count -= 1 messages = ai.chat(prompt=prompt, callback=send_message_event) # ← sync call ``` `AI.chat()` (`ai/ai.py`) does, in *both* branches: ```py try: loop = asyncio.get_running_loop() except RuntimeError: loop = asyncio.new_event_loop(); asyncio.set_event_loop(loop) return loop.run_until_complete(self.a_chat(...)) # no running loop: ok else: return loop.run_until_complete(self.a_chat(...)) # ← loop already running → RuntimeError ``` `generate_tasks` is always reached from a running loop (`asyncio.run(func(...))` in `sio_api_endpoint`, or an `async def` FastAPI route), so the `else` branch runs `run_until_complete` on the **already running** loop → `RuntimeError: This event loop is already running`. Worse: it is swallowed. `session.chat_action()` catches every `Exception`, logs it, and returns — so the caller sees a *successful* response with the status message frozen at `🔍 analyzing`. **Fix:** `messages = await ai.a_chat(prompt=prompt, callback=send_message_event)`. The same anti-pattern exists in sync tools executed inside the agent loop (relevant because any new task tool must not copy it): `tools/project_tools.py::project_search` → `ai.chat(...)` per document. Since `_execute_tool` awaits a *sync* callable inside the loop, `project_search` raises as soon as it has documents to validate. ### 4.2 🟡 `create_task` tool — works, but loses data `tools/create_task_tool.py`: ```py task = Chat( name=name, description=description, parent_id=current_chat.id if current_chat else None, files=files or [], # ← Chat has `file_list`, no `files` → silently dropped profiles=profiles or [], tags=tags or [], board=board, column=column, mode="task", # ← generate_tasks uses "chat"; mode drives is_refine ) ``` - `files=` is not a `Chat` field (it is `file_list`) → pydantic drops it. Only the first `Message.files` keeps the paths. - `mode="task"` makes the child a **document-refinement** chat (`_is_refine(mode)` in `chat_engine.py`), unlike sub-tasks produced by `generate_tasks` (`mode="chat"`). Inconsistent semantics between the two fan-out paths. - No `owner_project_id` fallback when there is no current chat. - Relies on `settings._active_session` / `session._current_chat`, injected by `SmolAgent._run_chat_loop` only when `config["current_chat"]` is present (it is, from `ChatEngine._execute_ai_response`). OK, but the injected "session" is a `ChatEngine`, not `CODXJuniorSession` — documented nowhere. - No branch/worktree per task, no priority/progress, no return of a *run* handle (only `task_id`). ### 4.3 🟡 `process_task` tool — `wait=True` is a lie ```py else: # wait == True if loop: loop.create_task(_process()) # fire & forget, NOT awaited else: asyncio.run(_process()) ... process_response = json.dumps({"status": "completed", "messages_count": len(task.messages), ...}) ``` Inside the agent runtime a loop **always** exists, so: - the task is scheduled and the tool returns immediately with `status: "completed"`; - `len(task.messages)` is read from a stale object (nothing was processed yet); - the `asyncio.Task` reference is not retained anywhere → it can be garbage-collected mid-flight (asyncio keeps only weak references). `wait=False` has the same retention problem, which is the one you actually need for parallelism. **Fix:** keep module-level `PENDING: set[asyncio.Task]`, `PENDING.add(t); t.add_done_callback(PENDING.discard)`, and for `wait=True` use `await asyncio.gather(*tasks)`. ### 4.4 ❌ No parallel tool execution inside an agent round `ai/smol/smol_agent.py::_run_chat_loop` supports **breadth** (the model may return N tool calls in one round) but executes them strictly sequentially: ```py # Separate cached / uncached... for tool_id, tool_call in uncached_calls.items(): run_context.checkpoint() tool_result = await self._execute_tool(...) ``` Limits: `LoopGuard(max_iterations, max_tool_calls)` with `DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS = 5`. So a model can request at most **5 tools per round**, executed in series. Parallelism must therefore live *inside* a tool (as `generate_tasks` does with `asyncio.gather`), not in the runtime. ### 4.5 ❌ Legacy / dead code | Item | Problem | |---|---| | `codx/junior/task_manager.py::TaskManager` | `from codx.junior.utils import extract_blocks` — `codx/junior/utils/__init__.py` **does not exist** → import error. No references found. Dead. | | `codx/junior/engine.py::generate_tasks` | Duplicate of the legacy session implementation (sequential `for` loop, no status message). `CODXJuniorSession` delegates to `ChatEngineActions`, so this copy is dead. | | `agents/git_issues_agent.py::create_subtasks` | Returns a hardcoded 3-item list. | ### 4.6 Shared-state hazards for real parallelism | Hazard | Detail | |---|---| | `ChatEngine` is stateful and shared | `switch_project()` mutates `self.settings` and `self.chat_knowledge`; `ChatEngineActions.chat_with_project` builds a **new** `ChatEngine` per call (good), but `AI(session=self)` points back at the mutable engine. Two concurrent tasks on different projects can corrupt each other. | | `settings._active_session` / `session._current_chat` | Global-ish mutable attributes on the settings object, overwritten by every SmolAgent run. Concurrent runs on the same project settings will cross-contaminate tool context. | | `ChatManager.save_chat` | Read-modify-write of one JSON file per chat. Safe across *different* chats; racy for concurrent writes to the **same** chat (e.g. `push_status()` from several `process_sub_task` coroutines). | | No concurrency limit | `asyncio.gather` fans out to **all** generated tasks at once — no semaphore, no per-parent budget check, no global cost guard (only per-chat `estimation_cost`). | | No working-tree isolation | Sub-tasks share the project checkout; concurrent `apply_file_changes` / `project_write_file` will collide. | --- ## 5. Ways a model *can* run parallel tasks today | Route | How | Verdict | |---|---|---| | **A. Ask for chat-level generation** | Nothing exposed as a tool; only `POST /api/chats/sub-tasks` / SIO `codx-junior-subtasks`. A model cannot trigger it. | 🧱 for models | | **B. `create_task` × N + `process_task(wait=false)` × N** | Enabled only if a profile lists the tools (`profile.tools`) — **no shipped profile does** (`analyst`, `software_developer`, `wiki` have no `tools` key). Bounded to 5 calls/round by `LoopGuard`. | 🟡 feasible, unreliable (§4.3) | | **C. Existing background/parallel building blocks** | `asyncio.gather` (`chat_engine_actions`, `knowledge_ai_search`, `change_manager`), `ThreadPoolExecutor` (`background.MAX_PROJECT_WORKERS=10`, `knowledge_milvus.parallel_enrich`, `context.parallel_validate_contexts`), SIO `SIO_POOL` (10 workers) | ✅ patterns to reuse for a proper fan-out tool | | **D. Git worktrees** | `create_pr_branch(worktree=True)` → isolated checkout, `pr_view.worktree_path`, `close_pr` / `abandon_pr` to merge/discard | 🟡 best available isolation primitive, never combined with tasks | | **E. Kanban/status** | `Chat.status` + `status_history`, board/column, `priority`/`progress` | ✅ ready to model task lifecycle, no automation runner | --- ## 6. What is missing for “a profile generates parallel tasks” Gaps, in priority order: 1. **A tool to decompose + fan out** (`create_tasks` / `generate_tasks` tool) → today `generate_tasks` is not in `TOOLS`. 2. **A tool to observe** children (`list_tasks` / `task_status`: id, name, status, progress, last visible answer, cost) → a coordinator model is blind today. 3. **A tool to fan in** (`wait_for_tasks(ids)` with `asyncio.gather`, timeout, per-task error capture) and inject the children's summaries back into the parent chat. 4. **Retained background tasks** + a concurrency semaphore + optional worktree per task. 5. **Fix the sync-AI-in-async bug** in `AI.chat` usage (§4.1) — any new async tool that calls AI is affected. 6. **Unify semantics**: `mode` (`chat` vs `task`), `file_list` vs `files`, `branch` (declared, never written). 7. **Profile ergonomics**: `profile.tools` is the only switch; nothing ships with task tools, and there is no “coordinator” profile. --- ## 7. Suggested minimal design (reusing what exists) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Profile: coordinator
tools: create_tasks, task_status, wait_for_tasks] --> B[create_tasks name, description, count] B --> C[semaphore N=3 · asyncio.gather] C --> D[per task: create_pr_branch worktree=true
store chat.branch + pr_view] D --> E[Chat(parent_id, mode=chat, tools from profile)
run chat_with_project inside its worktree] E --> F[task_status polls ChatManager: status, progress, last answer, cost] F --> G[wait_for_tasks → gather summaries] G --> H[parent answer aggregates results] ``` Concrete changes (all inside existing files, no new architecture): | File | Change | |---|---| | `engine/chat_engine_actions.py` | `await ai.a_chat(...)` in `generate_tasks`; wrap fan-out in `asyncio.Semaphore(get_max_parallel_tasks())`; serialise `push_status()` with an `asyncio.Lock` | | `tools/create_task_tool.py` | `file_list=` instead of `files=`; `mode` configurable, default `chat`; optional `create_pr_branch(worktree=True)`; return `worktree_path` | | `tools/process_task_tool.py` | module-level `PENDING_TASKS: set`; real `await asyncio.gather` for `wait=True`; optional `project_path`/worktree override | | **new** `tools/task_tools.py` | `create_tasks(list)`, `list_tasks(parent_id)`, `wait_for_tasks(ids, timeout)` — all read-only on `ChatManager`, so no AI call inside the tool | | `tools/__init__.py` | register the new tools + JSON schemas (scope `chat`) | | `ai/ai.py` | make `chat()` raise a clear error (or auto-detect) when called inside a running loop, to stop the silent-failure class | --- ## 8. Evidence index | Concern | File | |---|---| | Sub-task generation, status tracking, parallel creation | `codx/junior/engine/chat_engine_actions.py` | | Delegation (`generate_tasks`) | `codx/junior/engine/session.py` | | LLM tools | `codx/junior/tools/create_task_tool.py`, `process_task_tool.py`, `git_tools.py`, `__init__.py` | | Tool runtime, sequential loop, `LoopGuard`, context injection | `codx/junior/ai/smol/smol_agent.py`, `smol/constants.py` | | Sync/async bridge (**root cause §4.1**) | `codx/junior/ai/ai.py` | | Chat/task data model | `codx/junior/db.py` | | Persistence, tree traversal, board/column | `codx/junior/chat_manager.py` | | Profile → tools wiring | `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py::_resolve_profiles_and_model` | | API/SIO entry points | `codx/junior/api/chat.py`, `codx/junior/sio/sio.py` | | Parallel patterns to reuse | `codx/junior/background.py`, `knowledge/knowledge_ai_search.py`, `context.py` | | Dead code | `codx/junior/task_manager.py`, `codx/junior/engine.py`, `agents/git_issues_agent.py` | --- **Bottom line:** the *data model* (parent/child chats, board/column, status, cost, PR/worktree) and the *fan-out algorithm* (AI JSON split + `asyncio.gather`) are done; the *product surface* for a profile is not. Two blocking defects stand between today's code and profile-driven parallel tasks: **§4.1** (sync `AI.chat` inside async → silent failure) and **§4.3** (`process_task(wait=True)` returns before running). After those, the smallest useful increment is a `create_tasks` / `task_status` / `wait_for_tasks` tool trio plus a worktree-per-task option. Want me to write this up as a project doc (e.g. `api/docs/subtask-orchestration.md`) or go straight to the two bug fixes?

messages in real time. ``TOOL_END`` additionally carries the dual-response tool's

forensic audit trail.

When :class:`LoopGuard` stops the run (max rounds, max tool calls or stuck
loop), the run is **not** aborted. Instead the tool-usage value is summarised
by the project's knowledge/RAG model and appended to the assistant answer, so
the findings survive in the persisted message and the next iteration can
continue without re-running the same tools. The summary request is
best-effort, does not count towards the loop limits, and its token usage is
recorded separately with the ``tool-analysis`` tag.

Every round (iteration) computes its cost in cxjcoins from the provider usage
and the model price settings, accumulates it into the chat total and reports it

the model's own text: reasoning emitted between tool rounds plus the final

ChatEventBridge — attaches AgentRunContext events to the chat response message
and persists it on EVERY change (crash-safe).

      event also carries the tool's user-facing ``output`` so tool output can be
      rendered collapsed/hidden instead of polluting ``Message.content``.
    * ``response_message.lifecycle_events`` → list of :class:`LifeCycleEvent`

-----------
TOOL_END events carry the dual-response tool's user-facing ``output``
(``ToolResponse.user_response``). The bridge stores it on the matching
:class:`ToolEvent` (``ToolEvent.output``) instead of it being merged into the
chat content, so the client decides how to display it. Cached tool calls do not
re-emit output (the first execution already delivered it).

----------------------
On every event change the response message is:

    1. **Persisted immediately** via the ChatManager granular merge-safe
       methods (``add_message`` on first change, ``update_message`` after).
       If the process dies mid-run, every event received so far — including
       tool errors, run errors and aggregated analytics — is already on disk.
    2. **Streamed** to clients in real time via the EventManager so the UI
       can render tool progress live.

    Streaming callbacks may call :meth:`maybe_persist_stream` on every flush;
    the bridge persists the response message AT MOST once per
    ``STREAM_PERSIST_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`` (monotonic clock). A hard kill
    therefore loses at most that many seconds of streamed partial text while
    keeping disk I/O bounded.
